newsitem.title: JAPAN: BOJ says operation aimed to check rise in key rate.
newsitem.headline: BOJ says operation aimed to check rise in key rate.

text.p: The Bank of Japan (BOJ) conducted an accommodative money market operation on Wednesday to check a recent rise in the key short-term interest rate, a BOJ official told Reuters.

In reaction to the key overnight call rate staying at high levels on Tuesday and early on Wednesday morning, the BOJ supplied greater liquidity to the market than in previous sessions through its regular 9.20 a.m. (0020 GMT) operation, he said.
The official said the key overnight call rate stayed at high levels even after banks' seasonal fund-raising demand withered before and after the fiscal year-end.
Given the BOJ's accommodative operation, the key rate fell to 0.44 percent on Wednesday from Tuesday's 0.51 percent.
Before the operation, the key overnight call rate was offered at 0.53 percent while banks placed bids at 0.49 percent, traders said.
The BOJ injected 100 billion yen into the money market at 0020 GMT. The market had been in surplus by an estimated 180 billion yen.
Traders said the injection was a surprise to many market participants as they had expected the central bank to refrain from conducting an operation.
